title: Value of Coins and Bills: Counting Money to $100
seo_title: Grade 3 Money Worksheets: Value of Coins and Bills (TEKS 3.4C, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.4C determine the value of a collection of coins and bills
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 money worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.4C: count coins, count dollars and cents, collections of $1, $5, $10 and $20 bills with coins, make an amount and money word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Count bills first, then count on with the coins.
key_sub: Coins: 1¢, 5¢, 10¢, 25¢. Bills: $1, $5, $10, $20. Write cents with two digits: $4.05.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Coins: penny 1¢, nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢. Bills: $1, $5, $10, $20. 100¢ = $1.00.
  • Size does not tell the value: a dime is smaller than a nickel but worth more.
  • To count a collection, start with the bills, from greatest to least. Then count on with the coins: quarters, dimes, nickels, pennies.
  • Write dollars and cents with a point: $12.05 means 12 dollars and 5 cents.

Examples

Example

What is 3 quarters, 2 dimes and 4 pennies worth?

25, 50, 75

85, 95

96, 97, 98, 99

Answer: 99¢

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the coins, not their valueSay the value as you count: 25, 50, 60, 70 …
Thinking a nickel is worth more than a dime because it is biggerA dime is 10¢ and a nickel is 5¢.
Writing $4.5 for 4 dollars and 5 centsCents always use two digits: $4.05.

faq.a: Determine the value of a collection of coins and bills.

faq.q: Which coins and bills do Grade 3 students count?
faq.a: Pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters, and $1, $5, $10 and $20 bills.

faq.q: What is the best order to count money?
faq.a: Start with the bills from greatest to least, then count on with the coins from greatest to least.

faq.q: How do you write money amounts?
faq.a: Use a dollar sign and a decimal point with two digits for the cents: $7.40, $12.05. Amounts under a dollar can be written with the cent sign: 85¢.

items.q: How much money is shown?

items.q: How much money is shown?
items.e: Start with the $5 bill: $5. Count on the $1 bills: $6, $7. That is $7.00. There are 3 bills, but the $5 bill is worth 5 dollars.

items.q: How many cents are in 1 dollar?
items.e: 1 dollar = 100 cents. So $1 is the same as 4 quarters, 10 dimes or 100 pennies.

items.q: How do you write 1 dollar and 50 cents?
items.e: Write the $ sign, then the dollars, then a point, then the cents: $1.50. Don’t use the ¢ sign when you have a dollar or more.

items.q: How do you write 2 dollars and 5 cents?
items.e: The cents always use 2 places after the point. 5 cents is written 05, so the answer is $2.05. $2.50 would be 2 dollars and 50 cents.

items.q: How do you write 45 cents?
items.e: 45 cents is less than 1 dollar, so write the number and the cent sign: 45¢. $45 would be 45 dollars.

items.q: How much money is shown?

items.q: How much money is shown?

items.q: Which coins make 45¢?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Dimes: 35, 45. So 1 quarter and 2 dimes make 45¢. 4 dimes and 5 nickels make 65¢.

items.q: Which coins make 30¢?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Nickel: 30. So 1 quarter and 1 nickel make 30¢. 3 nickels make 15¢.

items.q: Which coins make 62¢?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50. Dime: 60. Pennies: 61, 62. So 2 quarters, 1 dime and 2 pennies make 62¢. 6 dimes and 2 nickels make 70¢.

items.q: Which coins make 81¢?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50, 75. Nickel: 80. Penny: 81. So 3 quarters, 1 nickel and 1 penny make 81¢. 8 nickels and 1 penny make 41¢.

items.q: Which coins make 56¢?
items.e: Dimes: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Nickel: 55. Penny: 56. So 5 dimes, 1 nickel and 1 penny make 56¢. 5 dimes and 6 nickels make 80¢.

items.q: Which coins make 90¢?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50, 75. Dime: 85. Nickel: 90. So 3 quarters, 1 dime and 1 nickel make 90¢. 9 nickels make 45¢.

items.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make 30¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first. 1 quarter and 1 nickel = 30¢. That is 2 coins. 3 dimes would also work, but that is more coins.

items.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make 40¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first. 1 quarter, 1 dime and 1 nickel = 40¢. That is 3 coins. 4 dimes would also work, but that is more coins.

items.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make 50¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first. 2 quarters = 50¢. That is 2 coins. 5 dimes would also work, but that is more coins.

items.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make 15¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first. 1 dime and 1 nickel = 15¢. That is 2 coins.

items.q: What is the fewest number of coins that make 60¢?
items.e: Use the biggest coin you can first. 2 quarters and 1 dime = 60¢. That is 3 coins. 6 dimes would also work, but that is more coins.

items.q: Valeria has these coins. She needs 50¢. Which one coin does she need?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Dimes: 35, 45. She has 45¢. 45 + 5 = 50, so she needs 1 nickel.

items.q: Ximena has these coins. She needs 60¢. Which one coin does she need?
items.e: Dimes: 10, 20, 30. Nickel: 35. She has 35¢. 35 + 25 = 60, so she needs 1 quarter.

items.q: Camila has these coins. She needs 60¢. Which one coin does she need?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50. Nickel: 55. Pennies: 56, 57, 58, 59. She has 59¢. 59 + 1 = 60, so she needs 1 penny.

items.q: Caleb has these coins. He needs 50¢. Which one coin does he need?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Dime: 35. Nickel: 40. He has 40¢. 40 + 10 = 50, so he needs 1 dime.

items.q: Which coins are worth the same as 1 quarter?
items.e: Count the nickels by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. 5 nickels = 25¢, the same as 1 quarter. 2 dimes are only 20¢.

items.q: Which coins are worth the same as 1 dollar?
items.e: Count the quarters: 25, 50, 75, 100. 4 quarters = 100¢ = $1.00. 10 nickels are only 50¢.

items.q: Which coins are worth the most?
items.e: 3 dimes = 30¢, 5 nickels = 25¢, 8 pennies = 8¢, 1 quarter = 25¢. So 3 dimes are worth the most. More coins do not always mean more money.

items.q: Which coins are worth the most?
items.e: 1 quarter = 25¢, 4 nickels = 20¢, 9 pennies = 9¢, 1 dime = 10¢. So 1 quarter is worth the most. More coins do not always mean more money.

items.q: Which coins are worth the least?
items.e: 4 nickels = 20¢, 1 quarter = 25¢, 3 dimes = 30¢, 6 nickels = 30¢. So 4 nickels are worth the least. One coin can be worth more than many coins.

items.q: Caleb has 2 dimes and 1 nickel. A pencil costs 30¢. Does he have enough money?
items.e: Dimes: 10, 20. Nickel: 25. He has only 25¢. 25¢ is less than 30¢, so no. He needs 5¢ more.

items.q: Diego has 1 quarter and 2 dimes. An eraser costs 40¢. Does he have enough money?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Dimes: 35, 45. He has 45¢. 45¢ is more than 40¢, so yes, it is enough.

items.q: Jayden has 2 quarters, 1 dime and 3 pennies. A toy car costs 65¢. Does he have enough money?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50. Dime: 60. Pennies: 61, 62, 63. He has only 63¢. 63¢ is less than 65¢, so no. He needs 2¢ more.

items.q: Harper has these coins. She wants a bag of grapes that costs 50¢. How much more money does she need?
items.e: Dimes: 10, 20, 30. Nickel: 35. She has 35¢. Count up from 35 to 50: 35 + 5 = 40, 40 + 10 = 50. That is 15 more. She needs 15¢ more.

items.q: Liam has these coins. He wants a jump rope that costs 75¢. How much more money does he need?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50. He has 50¢. Count up from 50 to 75: 50 + 10 = 60, 60 + 10 = 70, 70 + 5 = 75. That is 25 more. He needs 25¢ more.

items.q: Ximena has these coins. She wants a ruler that costs 60¢. How much more money does she need?
items.e: Quarter: 25. Dime: 35. Pennies: 36, 37. She has 37¢. Count up from 37 to 60: 37 + 3 = 40, 40 + 10 = 50, 50 + 10 = 60. That is 23 more. She needs 23¢ more.

items.q: Valeria has these coins. She wants a ball that costs 90¢. How much more money does she need?
items.e: Quarters: 25, 50. Dimes: 60, 70, 80. She has 80¢. Count up from 80 to 90: 80 + 10 = 90. That is 10 more. She needs 10¢ more.

items.q: A pear costs 45¢. An apple costs 30¢. Noah buys both. How much does he pay?
items.e: Add: 45 + 30. Count on from 45: 55, 65, 75. He pays 75¢.

items.q: A sticker costs 15¢. A pencil costs 25¢. Mia buys both. How much does she pay?
items.e: Add: 15 + 25. Count on from 15: 25, 35. Then add 5 more: 40. She pays 40¢.

items.q: A cookie costs 35¢. A juice box costs 40¢. Isaac buys both. How much does he pay?
items.e: Add: 35 + 40. Count on from 35: 45, 55, 65, 75. He pays 75¢.
